title: Copernicus Labs - Integration & Onramp Sandbox Profiling (Discovery)
summary: Initial integration discovery for Copernicus Labs evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Focus on onramp sandbox profiling, SDK compatibility (LangChain/LlamaIndex), gateway/proxy placement, per-route quotas and observability hooks. Security and VPC/KMS concerns surfaced; next steps include sandbox access, perf spreadsheet, and security docs share.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
Gateway/proxy placement and sidecar vs edge
Rate limits / quotas per-tenant and per-route
Security: KMS, SSO, audit logs, SOC2
next_steps: Redwood to provision sandbox onramp for Copernicus - Priya to send invite and creds
Alex to share pricing sketch for Dedicated pool + burst
Priya to run baseline token/latency profiling and upload spreadsheet
Redwood to send SOC2 + security primer and KMS integration notes
action_items: Priya Shah: create sandbox credentials and onboarding doc (due 2028-03-09)
Alex Moreno: send high-level pricing + dedicated commit options (due 2028-03-08)
Maya Li: provide sample traffic profile and expected qps/p50/p95 (due 2028-03-07)
Ben Ortiz: list compliance reviewers and desired audit window (due 2028-03-10)
Samir Patel: share current LangChain pipeline example and LlamaIndex usage (due 2028-03-06)
notes: Shared artifacts referenced: Copernicus-integration-deck.pdf (link), baseline-profiling-template.xlsx (link), redwood-security-primer.pdf (will be shared).
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-03-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Hale (CTO, Copernicus), Maya Li (Platform Eng), Ben Ortiz (Head of Security), Samir Patel (ML Eng), Olga Roman (DevOps), Luis Andrade (Redwood Solutions Eng, joined ~00:05)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, this is Alex from Redwood .. uh Moreno. coupla quick notes we have Priya the SE and Luis will hop in a bit later. can we do quick intros?
[00:12] Jordan: Jordan Hale, CTO at Copernicus, we build satellite-image analytics, lots of batch and some realtime callbacks.
[00:18] Maya: Maya Li, platform eng, I'll own the on prem / VPC side of things.
[00:23] Ben: Ben Ortiz, security, i'll be listening for compliance and KMS questions.
[00:28] Samir: Samir Patel, ML engineer, handles our LangChain pipelines and LlamaIndex vector store usage.
[00:34] Alex: great, thanks. goal for today is to map integration surface and decide sandbox profiling steps. Priya are you able to run through integration options?
[00:42] Priya: yeah, sure. um quick high level — Redwood gives three deployment modes: hosted API (fast to start), dedicated pool (reserved GPUs, predictable throughput), private (VPC or on-prem control plane). For integrations you can call the REST/SDK directly from app, or run a gateway/proxy at the network edge for routing, rate limiting, and local observability hooks.
[01:05] Maya: do you have an SDK for Node/python that's compatible with LangChain and LlamaIndex? we have existing chains.
[01:12] Priya: we do. official SDKs for python and node, plus a thin adapter for LangChain. for LlamaIndex folks we provide an embedders connector and a small example repo — sometimes names get munged in auto transcripts but it's generally straightforward.
[01:26] Samir: our current LangChain flows rely on synchronous calls and store embeddings in our vector db. curious about latency and token accounting when doing prefix caching and batching.
[01:36] Priya: good callout. Redwood runtime supports prefix/KV caching and continuous batching; you can tune batching window and max batch size per model. token accounting is exposed in per-request metadata, and we have token-level cost reports in the console.
[01:49] Ben: security question — if we use dedicated vs private, how does key management work? we need KMS/HSM and zero standing secrets.
[01:57] Priya: for dedicated we offer customer-managed KMS integration in the private networking options; on private deployment you can bring-your-own-KMS or HSM. Hosted API supports envelope encryption and managed KMS but we can discuss dedicated KMS for enterprise.
[02:12] Jordan: what about putting a gateway or proxy in front of Redwood? we want to do additional enrichment, tokenization and have local quota enforcement.
[02:20] Alex: common pattern is sidecar or edge gateway that handles auth, per-tenant quotas, and transforms. Redwood also supports an onramp gateway (our recommended proxy pattern) that forwards to the most cost or latency efficient model variant.
[02:33] Maya: do you support per-route quotas and rate limits per API key? we need to enforce bursts per-tenant.
[02:39] Priya: yep — per-route and per-api-key quotas. plus leaky-bucket burst settings. There's also metering hooks so your gateway can query remaining quota before processing.
[02:50] Samir: any built-in shimming for LangChain again? we've built custom retrievers and the LlamaIndex connectors are slightly different.
[02:59] Priya: we have sample code — a LangChain LLM wrapper that adapts Redwood streaming and function-calling. LlamaIndex connector is community-ish but maintained by our SDK folks; sometimes field tweaks are required for the vector store semantics.
[03:16] [Luis joins call, ~00:05 late]
[03:19] Luis: hey all, sorry for the delay. heard LangChain + LlamaIndex — we also have a tiny adapter for the llm.predict_stream interface to minimize friction.
[03:28] Jordan: thanks. on perf — we want to profile our typical chat path and a larger batch scoring job. what's the best way to run a realistic sandbox?
[03:36] Priya: recommend we provision a sandbox onramp tied to your account that mirrors a dedicated pool but with limits. Priya: we'll run baseline profiling with your traffic shape — p50/p95, token mix, sequence lengths — and return a spreadsheet showing latency, throughput, and cost-estimates across hosted/dedicated/private.
[03:55] Maya: what about network egress and residency? part of our compliance needs require data not to leave eu-west.
[04:02] Priya: we have regions and can pin to region. for private we support VPC peering or on-prem (air-gapped options) so data residency constraints are possible.
[04:12] Ben: audit logs — we need per-request logs for 13 months and immutable audit trails.
[04:18] Priya: for enterprise we offer extended retention add-ons and audit export to your logging system (S3 or SIEM). they can be delivered encrypted and with integrity guarantees.
[04:28] Jordan: are there known gotchas when running LlamaIndex retrieval-heavy workloads through Redwood?
[04:33] Priya: retrieval loops that call back for many short-context requests can blow up token costs and increase latency if not batched. we suggest using local caching in your gateway, batch retriever requests, or use KV caching on Redwood's runtime to cache decoder-side context.
[04:52] Samir: can KV cache be invalidated programmatically? for us the data changes weekly so we need TTLs.
[04:59] Priya: yes TTLs and explicit invalidation calls are supported in the runtime API.
[05:08] Maya: observability — we need traces that connect app spans to Redwood backend spans. is there an OpenTelemetry integration?
[05:15] Priya: yes we surface tracing headers; you can propagate a trace-id and see matching spans in Redwood's trace viewer, plus exports to your OpenTelemetry collector. sampling rate and span detail are configurable.
[05:28] Ben: what about PII redaction in logs and redaction at the token level?
[05:33] Priya: we have a redaction pipeline for logs and a token-filtering feature; in private modes you can disable logging entirely or route logs to your S3 with encryption.
[05:43] Alex: one thing to note — when you put a gateway in front, people often try sidecar versus central edge. sidecar gives you per-pod isolation but more ops. edge gateway simplifies centralized quota enforcement.
[05:58] Jordan: cost question — how does dedicated pricing look for predictable high throughput, and how do we account for burst capacity?
[06:05] Alex: high level: dedicated is monthly reserved GPU compute and you get predictable throughput; burst is charged as an overlay or we can offer burst buckets. I'll send a sketch but the profiling spreadsheet will show per-token cost at your observed distributions.
[06:18] Samir: for streaming responses and function calling, does Redwood stream tokens as they generate (server-sent events) or only after full chunk?
[06:25] Priya: streaming is SSE/Websocket style; supports partial tokens and function call streaming. for LangChain streaming wrappers we ensure compatibility.
[06:36] Olga: ops question — how do we manage deploys and rollbacks if we federate between hosted and dedicated models?
[06:43] Priya: routing is policy-driven; you can define canary cohorts, A/B routes, or failover to hosted if dedicated is saturated. that way you can do safe rollouts.
[06:55] Jordan: can Redwood do per-tenant model pinning? we might want customer X on a quantized variant for cost.
[07:02] Priya: yes model pinning per api-key/route is supported — you can route to costly high-quality model or cheaper quantized variant.
[07:10] Ben: on compliance, SSO/SAML and RBAC are required. do you integrate with our identity provider?
[07:16] Priya: we support SAML/SSO, SCIM provisioning and RBAC with roles and fine-grained permissions.
[07:23] Jordan: what are latency SLAs for dedicated? p95 numbers?
[07:28] Alex: depends on model and instance type; typical p95 for short prompts on a dedicated NVChain setup is ~70-120ms for optimized small models, larger contexts increase it. the sandbox profiling will give you real numbers.
[07:41] Samir: curious about endpoint telemetry — do you expose per-request token breakdown, execution time per stage (tokenize/encode/decode)?
[07:49] Priya: yes, per-request timing and token breakdowns are exposed; you can also get flamegraphs for hot kernels in the runtime if we do a deep dive.
[07:59] Maya: how invasive is the SDK change? we have a microservice in go that calls OpenAI-like endpoints; we prefer keeping the same interface.
[08:08] Priya: our REST is OpenAI-compatible-ish, and we also provide similarity in request/response shapes; we also have a Go SDK. Migration is typically minimal.
[08:16] Jordan: about the sandbox — what limits will be in place? number of concurrent connections, total tokens per day?
[08:22] Priya: sandbox will be rate-limited to protect the shared infra — we'll provide quotas per API key that mimic expected production. we'll also allow a higher limit for profiling windows.
[08:32] Alex: let's talk about observability hooks a bit more — common ask is pushing request traces to customer's collector, exposing metrics per-tenant and per-route, and integrating with Datadog/Prometheus.
[08:43] Priya: we have exporters for Prometheus and Datadog and recommend exporting aggregates; raw request streams can be sent to your SIEM for audit. we also have token-level cost metrics by tag.
[08:56] Ben: for audit retention and immutability, we prefer WORM S3. do you ship logs to our S3 with server-side encryption and object lock?
[09:03] Priya: yes, S3 export with SSE and optional object lock for immutability.
[09:09] [10:00 minutes into call — demo request thread]
[09:12] Samir: can we get an example of the LangChain wrapper with streaming and function calls? maybe a sample LLM chain?
[09:18] Priya: I'll drop a sample repo, it's called redwood-langchain-examples; it includes streaming chat, function-calling and an example with LlamaIndex retriever.
[09:27] Jordan: for the retriever loop, if we have thousands of little lookups per request, that's the worst case for tokens. you mentioned caching at the gateway — is that something Redwood provides or we build?
[09:36] Priya: you can do both. the gateway can cache retrieval responses and Redwood's runtime supports prefix caching and KV cache that's keyed on prompt fragments. caching at the gateway reduces upstream calls and costs.
[09:45] Olga: anything special for on-prem/private regarding model updates and rollouts? we need controlled updates.
[09:50] Priya: private deployments let you manage model artifacts; we support staged rollouts and an image registry approach so you can pin versions and roll forward/back. for air-gapped we provide an offline bundle.
[10:05] Jordan: regarding billing and cost transparency, can we get token-level traces per tenant for chargeback?
[10:12] Alex: yes chargeback is possible — you can tag requests and get per-tag cost breakdowns in the console and export CSVs.
[10:19] Ben: about data retention for training — do you retain content to improve models by default? we have policy against any training on customer data.
[10:27] Priya: by default hosted does not train on customer data; enterprise agreements can explicitly enable or disable training. we also support no-training contracts and guarantee in writing.
[10:38] Samir: small thing — do you have a rate-limit preflight API, like check token balance before executing a heavy call?
[10:44] Priya: yes quota check endpoints are available so you can avoid expensive requests when quota is low.
[10:50] Maya: how do you instrument streaming failures? we need to know if a stream was cut and whether to retry idempotently.
[10:57] Priya: streams have request IDs, and we maintain idempotency keys; resumable streams are possible in some flows, otherwise you can fall back to non-streamed call.
[11:08] [Crosstalk — someone laughed]
[11:12] Jordan: timeline — we're hoping to have a POC within 3 weeks and a security review shortly after.
[11:18] Alex: sounds reasonable. recommended steps: 1) Redwood provides sandbox and security docs; 2) Copernicus runs profiling workload; 3) Redwood returns profiling spreadsheet with hosted/dedicated/private comparisons; 4) decision on pilot.
[11:30] Maya: about quotas again — do you support hierarchical quotas (org->team->api-key)?
[11:36] Priya: hierarchical quotas yes, and metering at multiple levels.
[11:40] Samir: any known incompatibilities with LlamaIndex versions? we use 0.8.x at the moment.
[11:46] Luis: some older LlamaIndex call signatures changed around 0.7->0.8; our sample adapter targets a couple recent stable releases but we'll validate with your repo.
[11:58] Ben: security reviewers will want to run a short threat model — can you share your network diagrams and dataflow?
[12:05] Priya: yes we'll share an architecture diagram and a short security primer and include recommended network ACLs for VPC peering.
[12:12] Jordan: ok let's commit to the sandbox and profiling. do you need anything else from us to provision?
[12:18] Priya: sample traffic profile (qps, typical seq lengths, percent streaming vs batch) plus an account admin to grant API keys. Maya: you to share the profile.
[12:26] Maya: we'll collec– gather and send the profile by Monday.
[12:31] Alex: perfect. Any remaining hard blockers?
[12:35] Ben: we'll schedule a security review once we get the primer. also need to see KMS integration docs.
[12:41] Alex: we'll include KMS/HSM notes and SOC2 artifacts in the packet.
[12:46] Samir: curious re: debugging tooling — can we get a replay of a request with token-level logs if needed?
[12:52] Priya: yes with proper entitlements we can export full token logs for debug; these are gated and only available for enterprise with log export turned on.
[12:59] Jordan: okay last quick thing — we sometimes do offline scoring jobs that need GPU pools but don't require low latency. can dedicated handle mixed-latency workloads?
[13:07] Alex: yes dedicated pools can be partitioned or scheduled; we can allocate capacity for background batch jobs and reserve real-time lanes.
[13:17] [Wrap-up recap by Alex]
[13:20] Alex: recap — Redwood to provision sandbox onramp and drop sample repos and security primer. Copernicus to provide traffic profile and LangChain snippets. Redwood to run baseline profiling and share spreadsheet and pricing sketch. security review to be scheduled after docs.
[13:38] Maya: thanks all.
[13:40] Ben: thanks.
[13:42] Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with artifacts and the sandbox invite. bye.

End transcript.
